clue.text: Current controller in glasses, fascinating woman

parts.note: a witch is a bewitching, fascinating woman

explanation.surface: A man is transfixed by an enchanting woman wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests spectacles on the woman, but it means drinking vessels; 'Current' is electric current, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler-switch is the familiar flip-up-and-down electrical switch that turns a circuit's flow on or off.

clue.text: Prance about — what you do when hanging a picture?

parts.words: what you do when hanging a picture
parts.note: you put it up; in a down entry the 'up' is an instruction to write PUT IT from the bottom

explanation.surface: A light-hearted question about the bustle of hanging a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read upwards in the grid is PUT IT, so the entry literally is 'put it up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To titup is a dialect verb for moving in a lively, mincing or prancing way, like a frisky horse.

clue.text: Tropical skin disease making the afflicted pallid — not me! (11, three words)

indicators.note: something afflicted is damaged or disordered, so the letters that follow are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A sufferer, made pale by a tropical disease, prays to be spared it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pallid' looks like a symptom but is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mal del pinto, or pinta, is a tropical skin infection causing patches of discoloured skin, found in Central and South America.

clue.text: Thorny heart of problem that is grasped by bishop, variable

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only the middle of the next word is kept
something grasped is held inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: algebra uses x, y, z for variables

explanation.surface: A tricky problem that a bishop has to grasp, with a variable in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is Right Reverend, abbreviated with the doubled letter; the definition sits at the very front with no link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Briery means full of briars, prickly bushes, so it is a synonym of thorny.

clue.text: Cheeky talk on afternoon one's spent in Croatia

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for afternoon, as in a.m./p.m. style shorthand

explanation.surface: Someone gossips cheekily through an afternoon of spending money on a Croatian holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The lipa was the hundredth part of the Croatian kuna, a coin one could spend in Croatia.

clue.text: Being unselfish, say, loses when falling out

parts.note: e.g., 'for example', is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

indicators.note: falling out suggests tumbling into disorder, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A generous person loses out when quarrelling with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling out' reads as a quarrel but asks for the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoless describes someone with no self-centred pride, so being unselfish matches it as an adjective.

clue.text: Showy plant: see red one ran wild in rose garden

indicators.note: running wild means moving without order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written; these letters belong to the shuffle along with the answer
taken as written; these letters also belong to the shuffle

explanation.surface: A gardener points out a showy red plant that has spread wildly through the rose garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus RED and RAN, all jumbled, make ROSE GARDEN; 'one' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sego lily is a showy-flowered North American bulb plant, the state flower of Utah.

clue.text: Some stuffing for stew, as a bitter green paste

indicators.note: some of the stuffing means only part of the run of letters that follows is used

parts.note: the letters run across the word break from stew into bitter

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a bitter green paste goes into the stuffing for a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' seems to describe the paste but only lends two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the pungent green condiment, Japanese horseradish, served as a paste with sushi.

clue.text: Support drink — Islam working for what supports the opposite

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Islam's prohibition of alcohol set against someone who backs drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay starts with 'Support drink', and the definition reverses it: the answer backs the opposite of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotalism is the principle of total abstinence, the creed backing the opposite of drinking.

clue.text: Fan of film clubs alight over endless festival

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: C for clubs, the card suit
a fire that is still in is alight

explanation.surface: A film buff's clubs light up the screen at the end of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' in a down clue puts IN above the festival; a fire 'in' is one still burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is an enthusiast or connoisseur of cinema, a devoted film-lover.

clue.text: Porcelain style? Two with internal damage

indicators.note: internal means inside, so the second piece goes within the first

explanation.surface: Two porcelain pieces, damaged inside, raise the question of their style.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese export porcelain, richly decorated in blue, red and gold, named after its port.

clue.text: Half crazy (exactly!) about aged goddess

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other
half a word keeps the first part of its letters only

parts.note: gaga means crazy; '(exactly!)' stresses that precisely half is taken
ae. abbreviates Latin aetatis, 'aged', on memorials

explanation.surface: An aged goddess is half crazy, exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Crazy is gaga, and '(exactly!)' insists on precisely half of it; 'aged' is the memorial-stone abbreviation, not old.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaea, or Gaia, is the Greek earth goddess, mother of the Titans.

clue.text: Lime in compote I love

indicators.note: in means found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone declares their fondness for lime in a fruit compote.
explanation.walkthrough: Lime is the tree, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Teil is an old name for the lime or linden tree.

clue.text: Woman admitting recipe heavy on the cooking fat

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: R abbreviates recipe, from Latin recipe, 'take', on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook concedes her recipe uses too much fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy means containing lots of lard, the cooking fat, so it fits 'heavy on the cooking fat'.

clue.text: Palm, in which child receives a smack

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a + lip, which in Chambers can mean a kiss, and a smack is a loud kiss

explanation.surface: A child is smacked on the hand, the palm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' and 'smack' suggest a slap; the palm is a tree and the smack a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The talipot is a tall fan palm of Sri Lanka and southern India with huge leaves.

clue.text: Production of Tosca, new? —— 2 is fantastic!

definitions.text: Production of Tosca, new? —— 2 is fantastic!

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera-goer raves about a new staging of Tosca, scene two especially.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer fills the gap: the answer plus TWO, jumbled, gives TOSCA NEW. The '2' is not a cross-reference to 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is a scene in an opera, often a dramatic solo, exactly what a production of Tosca contains.

clue.text: Cox, one that's kept within the clock?

indicators.note: kept within means held inside, so one piece sits inside another

explanation.surface: A rowing cox is the one who keeps an eye on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox is the boat's steerer, not the apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A timoneer is a helmsman, one who steers, as a cox steers a rowing boat.

clue.text: One stocked by barrow boy? It's often under glass

indicators.note: stocked by means held in someone's stock, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a coster or costermonger sells fruit from a barrow

explanation.surface: A barrow boy stocks some item usually kept in a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under glass' suggests a greenhouse; it means beneath a drinking glass. A barrow boy is a London street trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is a small mat placed under a glass to protect the table.

clue.text: A head

parts.note: surface reading: any head, the top of the body
setter's reading: this was the Azed competition word, printed unclued; the text given is only its bare meaning, the Latin for head

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one answer is left without a clue for solvers to write their own; this entry carries only a plain gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Caput is Latin for head, used in anatomy for a knob-like head of a bone or organ.

clue.text: Seaside theatre venue often hired ape to juggle

indicators.note: juggling tosses items about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside show hires an ape as a juggling act.
explanation.definitionFit: The pierhead, the seaward end of a pier, is where seaside theatres were frequently built.

clue.text: 'Beloved brave' encompasses Longfellow's leading character

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another
the leading character of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial of the poet's name

explanation.surface: A literary note on whether Longfellow's hero is 'beloved' or 'brave'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' looks like Longfellow's hero, such as Hiawatha, but only means his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling is a term for someone dearly loved, so it is a synonym of beloved.

clue.text: Not a major thoroughfare? That's obvious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., a secondary British road below an A road

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as B-ROAD: in Britain, B roads are minor routes, as opposed to the main A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad means plain or unmistakable, as in a broad hint; B road is a lesser British road classification.

clue.text: Such as Turpin of old, affected after Bess's end

indicators.note: after places the piece before it second, following the piece named next
a word's end is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the name
camp means affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: Dick Turpin, the highwayman, performs a showy act after his horse Black Bess dies.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman; legend gives him a horse called Black Bess.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamp's archaic sense is a highwayman or robber on the road, which Turpin was.

clue.text: Prophetic Scot's gift is enveloped in occult chat

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so a piece goes within another
occult suggests mysterious working, so the letters are transformed

explanation.surface: A Scottish seer's gift lies hidden in mystical talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Taisch is the Highland Scottish term for second sight, the supposed gift of seeing the future.

clue.text: One of several marine ducks — wild orcs will swallow them regularly

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within another
wild means out of control, so the letters are disordered
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Fierce killer whales will gulp down sea ducks every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcs are Tolkien's goblins, though the surface suggests orcas.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoters are dark sea ducks of northern coasts, and there are several species.

clue.text: Car malfunctioning? Work inside revealing source of oil

indicators.note: inside means within, so a piece is placed in another
a malfunctioning part is not working properly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A mechanic works inside a broken-down car and finds an oil leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of oil' suggests a car leak, but it is coconut oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: Catlike creature, one member of Felidae — certain about that?

indicators.note: about means around, so the last piece wraps round what came before

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a catlike creature really belongs to the cat family.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: the creature is not in fact a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The suricate, or meerkat, is a small catlike mongoose of southern Africa.

clue.text: Of use to joiners — or railway workers?

parts.note: el is the American elevated railway

explanation.surface: A question of whether something serves carpenters or railwaymen.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmen means made of elm, a timber joiners use.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmen is an archaic adjective meaning made of elm wood, a timber woodworkers employ.

clue.text: Soul fan is anti music initially that rocks

indicators.note: something that rocks is shaken about, so the letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A soul music fan objects to music that rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Soul is the spirit, not the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: An animist believes that natural things have souls, so is a devotee of soul in that sense.

clue.text: Trim, having lost weight (not a little) without a doubt

indicators.note: having lost something means it has gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a tonsure is a monk's haircut, a trim
a ton is a weight that is not small

explanation.surface: A barber assures someone that a trim will certainly take weight off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure, used as an adverb, means certainly, so it can stand for 'without a doubt'.

clue.text: Doss down with English historian

parts.note: to bed down is to sleep somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps rough in the company of an English historian.
explanation.walkthrough: To doss down is British slang for sleeping somewhere makeshift.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People in the eighth century.

clue.text: Attendants from over the water present diners with a choice

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the things that do so, a plural noun

parts.note: the United States, across the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.surface: Waiters from abroad offer diners a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Menus are lists of dishes that give restaurant customers options to choose from.

clue.text: Excessive devotion that is shown by press back in May?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister when the puzzle appeared in 2019

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction

parts.note: to sit can mean to press or weigh on

explanation.surface: Fanatical devotion displayed by newspapers back in the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the month; with its question mark it is the 2019 Prime Minister, Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietism is exaggerated or affected piety, a show of religious devotion carried too far.

clue.text: People exercise them sometimes — leads required

definitions.text: People exercise them sometimes — leads required

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Dog owners walk their animals on leads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: owners exercise animals on leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Pets such as dogs are walked by their owners, on leashes, for exercise.

clue.text: Curtains with regular trimming and fresh catch?

indicators.note: trimming at regular intervals cuts every other letter away

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Curtains are hemmed neatly, and new fish are landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' and 'trimming' suggest sewing, but the trimming removes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a Scottish measure of fresh herrings just landed, about 37.5 gallons.

clue.text: Antique bureau twice dropping right out of sideboard

indicators.note: dropping something twice means removing two of it from the word

explanation.surface: An antique desk is twice taken out of a sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Desse is an old word for a desk or lectern, a writing bureau in antique form.

clue.text: Herbert and Morgan Duff? Sharing parents each may be the other's

definitions.text: Sharing parents each may be the other's

indicators.note: duff means faulty or useless, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the two names taken as written; 'and' simply joins them

explanation.surface: Two men, Herbert Duff and Morgan Duff, share parents.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff looks like a shared surname, but means 'useless' and signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother-german is a full brother, having both parents in common, so each of two such men is the other's.
